answer: An escrowed bounty makes each fake a paid target. A new identity locks 50 credits in escrow; anyone proving it a duplicate collects 20 credits, the rest burned. A trellis of reports ties each claim to its evidence, so a farm cannot hide puppets behind one another. Each pearl of proof must name a distinct identity key, blocking reuse. The walnut-shell trick fails because the bounty pays per identity: the kth fake still risks 50 credits, and silencing a farm means paying every member, so hush cost grows with size. Honest agents pay one bond and keep it by real work.
